feedback: Evidence so far: iterations 0 to 4 all ended off_track with max_error about 0.061 m on every track. Iteration 1 (12 mm, x = ±0.05 m) removed line loss on the oval and slalom, so span fixed coverage. Iteration 2 (16 mm, same span, kp 3.5, y 0.04) gave zero line loss on oval and slalom and the best score, 26.99, but max_error stayed at 0.061 m, so footprint and kp do not set the excursion. Iteration 3 (y 0.06 with ki 0.3) brought back line loss on the s-bend and slalom and left max_error at 0.061 m, so y = 0.06 is not useful. Iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.15 m, kp 4.4) gave the same max_error with higher control effort, so wheel_track does not set the excursion. I have built the integration to keep the iteration-2 controller and y = 0.04. I make no prediction for the mass 0.6 kg robot. Once its race is in, the next decision depends on its max_error and line_loss_events. If max_error falls below about 0.058 m with line loss at zero, yaw inertia is a real limit: keep the lighter mass and tune sensor span or footprint around it. If max_error stays at 0.061 m, the excursion is probably a start-up transient or fixed bias. The next geometry lever is then the start-up position, and I would ask you to propose it with a stated hypothesis. Sensor y below 0.04 m is untested and would be an exploration, not supported by evidence.
requested_changes: Keep the 16 mm footprint at x = ±0.05 m and y = 0.04 m, and test mass 0.6 kg as the single change, with wheel_track back at 0.12 m.
If max_error stays at about 0.061 m with line loss at zero, propose one start-up geometry change (for example sensor y slightly below 0.04 m, untested) and state the hypothesis it tests.
If line loss returns at mass 0.6 kg, revert to 0.8 kg and hold the iteration-2 geometry, since no other lever has shown a gain.
